title: Once they can grasp, young children may shake an object to hear if it sounds
summary: OpenStax says that once young children can grasp objects, they may shake them to see if the objects make sounds.
body: OpenStax Psychology, still on Piaget's first stage, says that once young children can grasp objects, they may shake them to see if the objects make sounds. The textbook offers that as learning by acting, not as a dated checklist item. It does not say which month the shake begins. A separate US list has its own line about banging two things together. It is not a dated checklist item.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 9.2 Lifespan Theories
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology web page, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports the sentence that children who can grasp may shake objects to see if they make sounds.
